question: Brazil Presidential Election
resolution_criteria:
A presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 4, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate that wins this election.

This market includes any potential second round. If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

"Other" means any option not listed here.
research:
The first round on 2026-10-04 settles everything except the runoff: Flávio Bolsonaro (about 47.0%) and Lula (about 45.2%) go to a second round on 2026-10-25. Every other listed name, and "Other", is effectively out. As instructed, I left out anything published after 2026-10-06.

## 1. Resolution source
- The criteria name the TSE as the official source (dadosabertos.tse.jus.br). I did not fetch that page, so I can't report a value from it directly. The first-round figures below come from news reports of the official count.
- 2026-10-05: First-round result: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) 47.03%, Lula (PT) 45.16%. Nobody passed 50%, so the runoff is on 2026-10-25. Abstention was 21.08%, the highest since 1998. [Americas Quarterly](https://www.americasquarterly.org/article/reaction-flavio-bolsonaro-and-lula-advance-to-brazils-presidential-runoff/)
- 2026-10-04: With more than 99% counted, Flávio had about 47% and Lula about 45%. [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/10/04/nx-s1-5981181/brazil-presidential-lula-bolsonaro)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-10-04: Only Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula are in the runoff. Tarcísio de Freitas, Jair, Michelle and Eduardo Bolsonaro, and Haddad were not on the first-round ballot.
- The minor first-round candidates, all of whom would count as "Other", are now eliminated: Augusto Cury 2.89%, Renan Santos 2.24%, Ronaldo Caiado 2.18%, Romeu Zema 0.27%, and seven others under 0.1%. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_Brazilian_general_election)
- The outcome is in practice a two-way choice between "Flávio Bolsonaro" and "Lula". Nothing settles the runoff yet.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- About 2026-10-05/06: Caiado and Zema endorsed Flávio for the runoff. Zema went first, and Caiado scheduled a joint announcement in Goiânia. [Gazeta do Povo](https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/cafe-com-a-gazeta/caiado-e-zema-anunciam-apoio-a-flavio-no-segundo-turno/)
- Sources disagree on Augusto Cury. One says he stayed neutral, while Terra says he backed Flávio with conditions. Renan Santos criticised both candidates and ruled out campaigning in the runoff. [Band B](https://www.bandab.com.br/politica/eleicoes-2026/quem-cury-caiado-renan-e-zema-vao-apoiar-no-segundo-turno-entre-flavio-bolsonaro-e-lula/), [Terra](https://www.terra.com.br/noticias/eleicoes/flavio-ou-lula-veja-quem-cada-candidato-a-presidente-derrotado-esta-apoiando-no-2-turno,723e71cf60c7b7ab4db8a79265b240afcmj9rw44.html)
- 2026-10-05: Analysts mostly favoured Flávio:
  - Brian Winter expects Flávio to win unless more damaging evidence comes out, for example linked to the Banco Master case.
  - Thomas Traumann calls Flávio "the clear favorite."
  - Alessandra Ribeiro expects a narrow Flávio win.
  - PL will be the largest party in both chambers: 28 of 81 Senate seats and 121 of 513 in the lower house. [Americas Quarterly](https://www.americasquarterly.org/article/reaction-flavio-bolsonaro-and-lula-advance-to-brazils-presidential-runoff/)
- 2026-10-03: Final pre-election polls had Lula slightly ahead or tied. Flávio's actual first-round result beat them.
  - Datafolha runoff: Lula 48% vs Flávio 45%. Some outlets report 47% vs 46% instead, and I couldn't confirm which is right.
  - CNT/MDA runoff: Lula 47.3% vs Flávio 43.1%.
  - Atlas/Bloomberg: Flávio 47.7% vs Lula 47.6%. [JB](https://www.jb.com.br/brasil/politica/2026/10/1061086-datafolha-aponta-lula-com-45-dos-votos-validos-e-flavio-bolsonaro-com-40.html), [O Povo](https://mais.opovo.com.br/jornal/politica/2026/10/04/pesquisas-de-vespera-mostram-lula-e-flavio-bolsonaro-em-empate-tecnico.html), [Bem Paraná](https://www.bemparana.com.br/eleicoes-2026/lula-x-flavio-veja-os-numeros-das-ultimas-pesquisas-antes-do-1o-turno/)
- I found no runoff polls published after the first round and before 2026-10-06.

## 4. Base rates
- Brazil has held runoffs in every presidential election since 2002. In 2022, Lula led round one 48.4% to 43.2% and won the runoff 50.9% to 49.1%. [Wikipedia 2022](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Brazilian_general_election)
- From my own background knowledge rather than the sources above: the first-round leader has gone on to win every Brazilian runoff since 1989, including 2014, when Dilma led round one 41.6% to 33.6% and won 51.6% to 48.4%. Lula has never come second in a first round and then won.
- The gap this time (about 1.9 points) is the smallest of any recent first round. The eliminated candidates hold about 7.7%, and they lean right or anti-PT.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not find a Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold price for the runoff that was published on or before 2026-10-06. The market coverage I found was all dated after the cutoff, so I left it out.
- Pre-election snapshot: a KuCoin item said Flávio led Lula on Polymarket, but the date was unclear. [KuCoin](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/fl-vio-bolsonaro-leads-lula-on-polymarket-ahead-of-brazil-s-2026-election)
- Older polling: Datafolha in March 2026 had Lula 46% vs Flávio 43%, with rejection around 46% for Lula and 45% for Flávio. [Yahoo/Reuters](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/flavio-bolsonaro-draws-even-lula-161733328.html)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The runoff on 2026-10-25, with TSE results expected the same night.
- Further endorsements from Cury, Renan Santos and regional governors, and where their voters go.
- Runoff polls from Datafolha, Quaest, AtlasIntel and others.
- TV debates and free broadcast airtime for the runoff.
- Possible new evidence in the Banco Master case or other scandals that analysts flagged as able to change the race.
- Whether turnout recovers from the record 21% abstention.
- The market resolves to "Other" only if no result is known by 2027-06-30, which looks remote given how fast the TSE counts.
